title: Unity Catalog, security and deployment boundaries
summary: Name the asset, identify the principal, test the allowed work, and keep connectivity separate from permission.
outcomes: Explain namespace and managed/external lifecycle responsibilities.
Reason about basic table-read privileges with representative identities.
Frame a cloud-labeled access and sharing validation without overclaiming.
startingAssumptions: The platform module separates account, workspace, metastore, compute and storage.
Use the cloud bridge if DNS, route or principal vocabulary is unfamiliar.
editorialRationale: An analyst access case builds from names through privilege conjunctions and negative tests; sharing/deployment are explicit additional boundaries.

concepts.definition: A naming hierarchy that distinguishes an object within its context.
concepts.example: quality.accepted.inspections names catalog quality, schema accepted and table inspections.

concepts.definition: A governed table whose underlying storage lifecycle remains externally managed.
concepts.example: Dropping an external table registration does not delete its cloud files.

concepts.definition: An identity such as a user, group or service principal to which permissions apply.
concepts.example: A scheduled pipeline identity needs different work permissions from a read-only analyst group.

concepts.definition: Permission to interact with objects within a named catalog or schema, without itself granting data read access.
concepts.example: USE CATALOG quality and USE SCHEMA quality.accepted accompany SELECT on the table.

concepts.definition: A deliberate check that an identity is prevented from an action outside its intended permissions.
concepts.example: The reporting analyst can read accepted metrics but cannot modify raw inspections.

concepts.definition: Whether the relevant origin can connect through the required path to the destination service.
concepts.example: The table grant can be correct while a restricted source endpoint is unreachable.

concepts.definition: The external consumer identity or organization authorized to receive a defined shared data scope.
concepts.example: An approved supplier receives a subset of quality results, not automatic access to all raw inspections.

concepts.definition: The permissions and conditions that actually apply to the acting principal in the tested context.
concepts.example: A group grant may exist but the scheduled identity or inherited scope can differ from expectations.

concepts.definition: A query-time rule controlling the value returned for a column.

selfQuestions.prompt: Write the recommendation without granting blanket administration.
selfQuestions.modelAnswer: Verify the analyst’s effective identity and qualified object, then check parent usage and SELECT plus execution/error context. If USE SCHEMA is the identified gap, ask the authorized owner for that scoped correction and repeat both the allowed read and prohibited raw modification; investigate network evidence separately when relevant.
selfQuestions.reasoning: It separates known privilege gaps from other possible failures and validates scope rather than maximizing access.

beats.title: A three-part name locates an asset
beats.outcome: Read catalog.schema.object without treating it as an access grant.
beats.explanation: Read quality.accepted.inspections as catalog, schema and object. This [[dbxfe-m06-names-concept|namespace]] tells you which asset is intended; it does not grant permission or prove that another workspace points at the same environment. Unity Catalog organizes governed objects, while the workspace supplies collaboration context. Confirm both before diagnosing an apparently missing or different table.

samajh.text: Building, floor aur room number address ko precise banate hain. Address pata hona room mein enter karne ki permission nahi hai. Catalog, schema aur table bhi location clear karte hain; kaun read kar sakta hai woh alag rule hai. Galat building mein same room number ho sakta hai.
samajh.mapping: Address hierarchy models names; entry permission models authorization.
samajh.boundary: Unity Catalog scope and inheritance are software rules beyond a building analogy.

handbook.markdown:
A fully qualified name reduces accidental dependence on a session’s default catalog or schema. In this example quality is the catalog, accepted the schema and inspections the table. The name tells the reader which logical object is requested, while a metastore/workspace relationship supplies governance context.

If two colleagues see different results, check the actual environment, effective object and data version before blaming the calculation. Similarly, a missing-object error can reflect a wrong name or context as well as access restrictions. Preserve the exact safe error and qualified identifier. Do not turn an unknown object into a new table just to make a demo run.

Unity Catalog governs more than tables, and not every securable uses this same three-level shape. Storage credentials, external locations and shares have their own positions and responsibilities. This beat teaches the table path used by the course, not a universal object-layout rule. The next beat separates object governance from underlying file lifecycle, because a clear name still does not say who is responsible for the stored bytes.

beats.recap: The name identifies the requested asset; access and storage lifecycle remain separate.
beats.changeNote: New teacher-first explanation and worked visual; earlier lesson completion does not complete this beat.

beats.title: Who manages the files after the table changes?
beats.outcome: Distinguish managed/external lifecycle and business ownership.
beats.explanation: Managed and external tables differ in file lifecycle responsibility, not simply in whether they have a governed name. An [[dbxfe-m06-lifecycle-concept|external table]] can be governed through Unity Catalog while its cloud files have separate owners and policies. Also distinguish the technical object owner from the business metric owner: permission to administer a table does not decide what “defect rate” means.

handbook.markdown:
Begin a lifecycle review with object type and storage path ownership. A managed table delegates its underlying lifecycle to the platform’s managed behavior, including defined recovery and eventual deletion rules. An external table registers data whose file lifecycle is managed separately. That does not make external tables ungoverned, nor does a governed registration automatically control every external writer.

For Cinderline, ask who can alter the raw object path outside the intended table interface, who owns retention, and what happens when a table is dropped or renamed. A direct cloud deletion can affect readers regardless of a neat catalog structure. No deletion or permission change is performed by this exercise.

Separately assign metric ownership. A platform administrator may be able to administer the table but should not silently redefine the unit defect denominator. The quality lead approves business meaning; data/platform owners implement and operate it. Lineage and documentation help locate dependencies, but do not replace these decisions. Record recovery expectations from the actual target configuration rather than promising a default number of days as an immutable guarantee.

beats.recap: Governance, file lifecycle and business meaning have different owners and evidence.
beats.changeNote: New teacher-first explanation and worked visual; earlier lesson completion does not complete this beat.

beats.title: Test the identity that will do the work
beats.outcome: Distinguish human, group and workload principals in a proposed access matrix.
beats.explanation: A [[dbxfe-m06-principals-concept|principal]] is who or what acts. An administrator’s successful query is not evidence for the analyst or scheduled job. Define the work first: analysts read the approved metric; a pipeline identity writes accepted output; a steward investigates quarantine. Then test those identities with the intended scope rather than borrowing a broad account to make everything pass.

handbook.markdown:
Separate authentication from authorization. Authentication establishes the acting identity; authorization evaluates permitted actions. A service principal used by a scheduled pipeline may not have the same grants, credentials or workspace access as the human who authored the notebook. Record the effective execution identity, not only the person who clicked Run.

An access matrix should state purpose and scope before translating it into product privileges. The analyst needs the approved report, not every raw source. The pipeline needs defined writes, not account administration. The steward may need restricted exception evidence, which can contain sensitive raw values. Appropriate groups can simplify administration, but group membership and inherited grants must still be verified.

Use a representative non-administrator identity for acceptance tests. A successful administrator demo establishes a preliminary functional path, not least-privilege validation. Also test an intentionally prohibited operation. This module’s examples remain proposed and synthetic; no real principal is created and no cloud permission is changed. The next beat works through the basic table-read conjunction under the documented privilege model.

beats.recap: Validate the actual acting identity and purpose, not a convenient administrator.
beats.changeNote: New teacher-first explanation and worked visual; earlier lesson completion does not complete this beat.

beats.title: Three basic grants work together
beats.outcome: Evaluate parent usage and table-read requirements as a conjunction.
beats.explanation: For the basic table read, SELECT works with USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA. A [[dbxfe-m06-read-concept|usage privilege]] lets the principal use the containing namespace; it does not itself expose every row. The visual toggles the missing parent grant while keeping the table unchanged. These are basic object requirements, not the entire workspace, compute, policy and network setup.

handbook.markdown:
Evaluate the conjunction explicitly: table SELECT, parent USE SCHEMA and parent USE CATALOG. If one basic requirement is absent, the table-level read condition is not satisfied. Conversely, having those grants does not prove that the principal can reach the workspace, use the intended compute, pass additional policies or access every underlying resource through every path.

In our fictional matrix, the missing schema usage is the identified gap. The responsible owner should review and grant only the intended scope through the approved process. Then repeat the read as the analyst and repeat a prohibited write. Do not treat the diagram as evidence of a configured environment.

Check effective privileges, including group membership, inheritance and ownership. A broad parent grant can apply to more assets than an individual table grant. The current reference describes Privilege Model 1.0; older metastores may differ. Avoid copying tutorial ALL PRIVILEGES statements as a shortcut. Fine-grained DML privileges are marked Beta in the reviewed page and are not a general prerequisite here. The purpose is a teachable minimum table-read model with its limits clearly stated.

beats.recap: Parent usage plus table SELECT is a basic conjunction, not a full deployment guarantee.
beats.changeNote: New teacher-first explanation and worked visual; earlier lesson completion does not complete this beat.

beats.title: A useful test includes a denial
beats.outcome: Explain the evidence gained by allowed and prohibited operations.
beats.explanation: An allowed read proves one intended path works. A [[dbxfe-m06-negative-concept|negative access test]] checks an important boundary: the same analyst should not modify raw inspections. Run both with the actual principal and record the scope. If the prohibited write succeeds, the read success is not enough to call access correct; inspect inherited grants or ownership that may have broadened it.

handbook.markdown:
Choose negative tests from the stated access matrix, not arbitrary destructive operations. A controlled nonproduction test or safe permission validation can establish whether a prohibited capability is available without damaging real data. The important fact is which identity and object/action were evaluated. This course performs no actual grant or write.

A negative test can reveal inherited privilege, group membership, ownership or use of the wrong identity. If an analyst test was accidentally run as an administrator, both success and denial conclusions may be meaningless for the intended consumer. Capture that context alongside the result.

Do not call one denied operation proof that the whole system is secure. It is bounded evidence for a named policy condition at a time. Re-test after material membership, ownership or policy changes. A customer-facing statement should be precise: “The approved read and this prohibited modification were checked using the intended consumer identity.” That is more useful than a blanket assurance based on a working demo. The next beat adds the independent network boundary.

beats.recap: Correct access means intended work succeeds and relevant prohibited work remains denied.
beats.changeNote: New teacher-first explanation and worked visual; earlier lesson completion does not complete this beat.

beats.title: A grant cannot repair an unreachable path
beats.outcome: Separate access-control and connectivity diagnosis in AWS context.
beats.explanation: Permission and [[dbxfe-m06-network-concept|network reachability]] are independent. A granted table read may still fail through an unavailable execution path; a reachable endpoint may deny the request. On AWS the classic/serverless compute boundary also changes who operates the path. State origin, destination, identity, region and intended action before asking a specialist to validate the deployment.

samajh.text: Key hai par building tak road blocked hai toh key badalne se help nahi hogi. Road open hai par key wrong hai toh bhi andar nahi ja sakte. Network path aur permission dono check karo, aur kis origin se request ja rahi hai woh clear rakho.
samajh.mapping: Road models connectivity; key models authorization.
samajh.boundary: Cloud identity, endpoint and policy layers are more complex than a physical lock.

handbook.markdown:
Begin with the actual requesting workload. A user’s browser, a classic compute resource and a serverless job may have different network origins and effective identities. An approved diagram must name the chosen cloud and region, resource locations, DNS/egress ownership and the supported connectivity mechanism.

For Cinderline’s restricted source, ask which fields may leave the source, which destinations are permitted, who controls the path, and how operations will detect and handle failures. A serverless network feature may depend on region, resource type and entitlement; the current documentation also includes networking cost considerations. A generic product diagram is not customer approval.

Keep the response bounded: “We will verify this path and principal in the selected AWS model.” Do not transpose Azure private-resource names or assume another cloud’s setup is equivalent. If the conceptual video uses Azure, treat it as a governance overview and return to AWS sources for deployment specifics. The optional canonical cloud bridge explains DNS, routing and service-denial evidence at the exact point needed.

beats.recap: Name the origin/path and the permission separately before diagnosing the deployment.
beats.changeNote: New teacher-first explanation and worked visual; earlier lesson completion does not complete this beat.

beats.title: Sharing adds a recipient and a lifecycle
beats.outcome: Define external sharing scope and limits before treating an internal grant as sufficient.
beats.explanation: An internal analyst grant does not define an external sharing arrangement. Name the [[dbxfe-m06-sharing-concept|data recipient]], data subset, purpose, freshness, allowed use and revocation owner. Current sharing mechanisms provide controlled access paths, but revoking future access cannot erase copies a recipient already obtained. Make that lifecycle boundary part of the agreement rather than hiding it behind “secure sharing.”

handbook.markdown:
Describe the sharing relationship before selecting a feature: provider, recipient, data classification, subset, permitted purpose, refresh expectation, retention obligations and revocation/audit owner. An internal group grant is a different relationship from a partner consuming data through an external sharing protocol.

The current official delta-sharing URL redirects to the OpenSharing overview. This module records that current source naming without renaming historical lesson IDs or implying that every old feature behaves identically. The chosen protocol path, asset type, recipient client, region and feature support must be verified for the actual deployment.

An approved access path can be revoked, but data already copied by the recipient is not automatically recalled. Address that through the applicable agreement and operating process; do not turn a permission toggle into an erasure guarantee. Lineage can help inspect dependencies but has documented coverage limits, including unsupported patterns. It is evidence to use with other records, not proof that every external use is known. The course uses a fictional supplier case and performs no sharing action.

beats.recap: Sharing is a scoped relationship with a recipient, lifecycle and honest revocation limits.
beats.changeNote: New teacher-first explanation and worked visual; earlier lesson completion does not complete this beat.

beats.title: Make the consumer test concrete
beats.outcome: Write a bounded diagnosis and acceptance statement for a failed analyst query.
beats.explanation: An analyst has SELECT, can open the workspace, but cannot read quality.accepted.inspections. Inspect [[dbxfe-m06-transfer-concept|effective access]]: identity, qualified object, parent usage, execution context and exact error. If USE SCHEMA is missing, propose the narrow correction, then test the allowed read and denied raw modification. Keep network validation separate if the evidence points there.

handbook.markdown:
A useful diagnosis narrows uncertainty instead of escalating privileges until an error disappears. Start with the effective principal, environment and exact object. Then check the basic table-read requirements and whether inherited grants/ownership change the expected scope. Inspect execution access and connectivity according to the actual error.

The proposed correction in this fixture is parent schema usage, not account administration or a copy of the raw table. After the authorized owner applies it in a real setting, use the intended analyst to test the approved read and a safe negative access condition. Record results and limitations. A successful administrator run remains separate preliminary evidence.

For the security lead: “We identified a missing basic parent privilege and will validate the corrected consumer path plus the intended denial. This does not yet certify every network, sharing or regulatory requirement.” That sentence is deliberately bounded without being evasive. Review the canonical cards on naming, owners, privileges and cloud boundaries, then choose the researched extensions about discovery, inheritance and lineage. No real privileges have been changed by this learning module.

beats.recap: A concrete consumer test states identity, object, allowed work, denied work and limits.
beats.changeNote: New teacher-first explanation and worked visual; earlier lesson completion does not complete this beat.

extensionCards.prompt: Does BROWSE mean a principal can SELECT the data?
extensionCards.answer: No. BROWSE supports discovery and metadata/access requests; data read has separate requirements.
extensionCards.explanation: The current privilege reference distinguishes catalog discovery from SELECT and parent usage requirements. Seeing an asset name is not proof that its rows are readable.
extensionCards.whyItMatters: Avoid confusing findability with permission: a name in the catalog browser is not a readable table.

extensionCards.prompt: Why review a schema-level SELECT grant differently from one table grant?
extensionCards.answer: It can inherit to current and future tables/views in that schema under the documented model.
extensionCards.explanation: A broad parent grant may exceed the intended one-report scope and can affect assets created later. Inspect effective access and the governing privilege model rather than assuming only today’s table is covered.
extensionCards.whyItMatters: Access changes can have future scope as well as immediate effects.

extensionCards.prompt: An analyst sees a masked contact value. What additional evidence is needed before saying access is correctly governed?
extensionCards.answer: Test the actual allowed and denied identities, applicable rows/columns and supported access paths; a masked display alone is not an encryption or universal-access guarantee.
extensionCards.explanation: A [[dbxfe-m06-extension-column-mask-concept|column mask]] changes what a permitted query returns for a field. A row filter instead changes which rows are returned. In the fictional case, a reporting analyst may see a redacted supplier contact while an approved steward sees the original. Verify the policy’s actual identity conditions and data types, then test both outcomes. A screenshot under one user is only one observation. Current documentation lists runtime and interface limits, including restrictions on path-based access. Do not describe a query mask as encryption of stored bytes or assume it secures separately accessible copies. This extension configures no real policy.
extensionCards.whyItMatters: Extends grant reasoning to returned data while keeping the enforcement boundary explicit.

extensionCards.prompt: Does a lineage graph prove every dependency or access path was captured?
extensionCards.answer: No. Coverage has documented operation and object limitations.
extensionCards.explanation: The reviewed source lists cases such as path-based column references and some UDF patterns with incomplete capture. Treat visible lineage as useful evidence, and investigate unrepresented paths rather than inferring they do not exist.
extensionCards.whyItMatters: An incomplete graph should not become a universal governance guarantee.

recap.title: Name, identity, permission, path and lifecycle
recap.markdown:
**Locate the object → identify the principal → check scoped grants → test allowed and denied work → validate the cloud path → govern sharing/lifecycle.** Core cards preserve their existing IDs and review history; extension cards are an explicit additional choice.

**Next learning action:** continue with D2 Identity, authorization and audit (`#/module/dbxfe-identity`), which follows the principal you tested here through OAuth, service principals and audit events.

appliedTask.title: An analyst, a parent grant and a supplier
appliedTask.prompt: The analyst lacks USE SCHEMA but has SELECT. An admin demo works. The team also wants to send a supplier the report. Write the narrow next steps and one sharing limit.
appliedTask.modelAnswer: Verify identity/object/context, ask the authorized owner to correct the missing schema usage, and test the intended analyst’s read and prohibited raw modification. Scope supplier sharing separately by recipient, subset, purpose, freshness and revocation owner; revoking future access does not erase already obtained copies.
appliedTask.reasoning: Admin success does not validate the consumer. Internal grants do not establish an external sharing contract, and technical access controls have lifecycle limits.
